summary: The bottom-up level result contains every node value, so producing it requires linear time. Breadth-first traversal with whole-level prepending matches that bound and uses width-proportional traversal space.

optimality.argument: For an n-node tree, the returned nested lists contain exactly n values. Materializing those values requires Omega(n) time. The current traversal enqueues and dequeues each node once, appends each value once, and prepends each completed level to a deque in O(1) time, giving O(n) total time and O(w) auxiliary queue space excluding the output.

replacement_checks.evidence: The required nested result explicitly contains all n node values, so it cannot be produced in o(n) time.
Each node enters and leaves the breadth-first queue once, and each complete level is prepended once to the result deque.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover a branching tree, a one-node tree, and an empty tree; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
